title: CTAB DNA Extraction Protocol of P. pruinosa
author: Unknown
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.icgcatw
materials: Estimate the volume of the aqueous phase.

steps.title: Prepare CTAB extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Make CTAB buffer according to the attached recipe, then add polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) and β‑mercaptoethanol; after addition the buffer is stable for only 2–3 days. Dissolve the PVP by placing the solution in a water bath for 10–20 min without shaking (shaking causes excess bubbling). Verify all calculations if scaling the recipe.

steps.title: Collect and label tissue tubes
steps.instruction: Retrieve frozen plant tissue from the –80 °C freezer and keep it on dry ice to prevent thawing. Label 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes with a Lab Marker (Sharpie markers bleed when alcohol contacts them).

steps.title: Transfer frozen tissue
steps.instruction: Using force‑filled forceps, place 80–100 mg of frozen tissue into each labeled tube (exact mass is not critical as long as tissue stays frozen). If the tissue begins to thaw, submerge the tube briefly in liquid nitrogen to refreeze. Between samples, dip forceps in bleach water, rinse in clean water, and dry. Record whether any tissue remains unused.

steps.title: Grind tissue in liquid nitrogen
steps.instruction: Add liquid nitrogen to the tube and grind the tissue with a blue pestle, keeping the material frozen throughout. Use a fresh pestle for each sample. Soak each pestle in bleach water for at least 20 min before rinsing and autoclaving.

steps.title: Add CTAB buffer and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of the prepared CTAB buffer to each tube and vortex or flick until the tissue is fully suspended (no clumps). Turn on the water bath, set it to 65 °C, ensure several centimeters of water are present, and place the tubes in the bath for at least 30 min, mixing once after 5 min. Tubes may remain a few extra minutes if needed. Before starting, confirm you have sufficient volumes of CTAB buffer, isopropanol, 70 % ethanol, 95 % ethanol, and TE buffer; consult the recipe if any are low.

steps.title: Label downstream tubes while incubating
steps.instruction: During the CTAB incubation, label the tops and sides of clean 2 mL tubes with a VWR marker using capital letters for sample IDs, add the date, and wrap each tube with tape to protect the marker after freezing.

steps.title: Add RNase A and second incubation
steps.instruction: After the 30‑minute CTAB incubation, add 1.5 µL RNase A to each tube and incubate at 37 °C for 15 min. Process samples in batches of 10–20 for efficiency.

steps.title: Extract with chloroform
steps.instruction: Transfer the tubes to a fume hood, add 900 µL chloroform to each, and mix gently by shaking. Change gloves immediately if chloroform contacts skin. Avoid dripping chloroform onto the tube walls, as it can cause label bleed‑through.

steps.title: Centrifuge to separate phases
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes for 10 min at 12 000 r/min.

steps.title: Transfer aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Carefully pipette the upper (aqueous) layer into a newly labeled tube, avoiding any chloroform (bright‑green) carry‑over. Dispose of chloroform waste in a glass bottle marked for chemical waste.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with ammonium acetate and isopropanol
steps.instruction: Add 0.08 × sample volume of cold 7.5 M ammonium acetate, then add 0.54 × sample volume of cold isopropanol. Invert the tube 20–30 times to mix. Ensure isopropanol and ethanol are stored in the freezer beforehand; ammonium acetate should be kept cold in the refrigerator.

steps.title: Incubate on ice
steps.instruction: Place the tubes on ice for 30–40 min to allow DNA precipitation.

steps.title: Discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Remove and discard the supernatant into an isopropanol waste jar, taking care not to disturb the DNA pellet.

steps.title: Second spin to dry pellet
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes again for 1 min at 12 000 r/min.

steps.title: Wash pellet with 70 % ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 700 µL of 70 % ethanol to each tube and invert 5–10 times to wash the pellet.
